subject: Request: Segregated-service evidence & architecture walkthrough
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@veridian.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@veridian.com
Date: 2027-12-05T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Segregated-service topology + evidence for SOC 2 / SIG

Diego,

Thanks for taking this — Veridian's audit team is preparing for an upcoming SIG + CAIQ review and we need a compact package describing how Redwood isolates Dedicated and Private deployments from our multi-tenant hosted environment. Specifically we need:

- A short architecture overview (1 page) that clearly states the isolation model for Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- Network diagrams (layered): control plane, data plane, and customer-facing ingress/egress for both deployment types. Visio or PDF is fine.
- Mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls (we'll be focusing on scoping for network segregation and tenant isolation).
- Any runbooks or playbooks that describe tenant onboarding/offboarding and tenant eviction in an emergency.

Can you deliver a draft by Dec 8th? Also please include a suggested 60-min walkthrough slot so our auditors can ask follow-ups.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Security Engineer, Veridian Systems

Attachment: (none in this message)

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@veridian.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Segregated-service topology + evidence for SOC 2 / SIG

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a concise package that covers the items below. Proposed contents (deliverable v1):

1) One-page isolation summary (PDF): high-level statement of our isolation guarantees and where Dedicated vs Private sit relative to the hosted plane.
2) Three diagrams (PDF/Visio): control-plane partitioning, data-plane demarcation, and tenant egress/egress filtering for Dedicated and Private.
3) SIG/CAIQ mapping spreadsheet: controls called out with artifact pointers (network ACLs, KMS boundaries, tenant keying notes).
4) Onboarding & eviction runbook (markdown + PDF) — steps and artifact locations.

Proposed timeline: Draft to you by 2027-12-08 EOD PT; final by 2027-12-10 after your review.

Walkthrough: we can offer 2027-12-09 at 10:00 PT or 2027-12-10 at 14:00 PT. Please confirm which works for your auditors.

I'm including Kimberly and Karthik to help with the netmap and CAIQ mappings.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: segregation_summary_v1.pdf (stub), private-dedicated-netmap.vsdx (stub)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@veridian.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-06T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Segregated-service topology + evidence for SOC 2 / SIG

Quick technical notes to include in the deliverable:

- Control plane: single, customer-oblivious control plane; Dedicated control plane endpoints are logically partitioned and access-controlled via customer-scoped service accounts and RBAC. Private deployments optionally run customer-managed control plane components in VPC/air-gapped environments (we'll mark this as an optional configuration).

- Data plane: inference workloads run in isolated GPU pools. For Dedicated, pools are reserved and tagged per-customer; for Private, all compute and storage (if on-prem) are customer-owned.

- Network enforcement: default-deny security groups, egress filtering for external artifact access, eBPF-based runtime policing in hosted edges, and strict route tables on Dedicated VPCs.

- Tenant lifecycle: onboarding uses enrollment API + signed contract artifact; offboarding includes cache flush, key revocation, and ephemeral data retention tasks. Eviction playbook includes last-resort snapshot + SANITIZE steps.

I'll attach a compressed CAIQ mapping workbook (sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx) and a short list of artifact IDs we'll point to in the spreadsheet.

-Kim
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx (stub)

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@veridian.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-07T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Segregated-service topology + evidence for SOC 2 / SIG

Alex — delivering the draft package now. Attached: segregation_summary_v1.pdf, private-dedicated-netmap.vsdx, sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx. Short notes:

- The one-page summary states our default-hosted isolation model (multi-tenant runtime with strong egress + prefix caching separation), Dedicated reserved-pool guarantees (GPU pool reservation, per-customer VLAN tagging where deployed), and Private options (VPC on-prem and customer-managed control plane).

- The diagrams show control-plane/out-of-band channels, labeled subnets and trust boundaries, and a short example of tenant traffic flow (customer request -> routed edge -> isolated compute pool -> KMS call for model keys).

- The SIG/CAIQ workbook maps each control to evidence artifacts. Where we reference operational artifacts (runbooks, onboarding tickets, attestation hashes) we included SharePoint URLs and internal artifact IDs. See links below.

Requested walkthrough confirmed for 2027-12-09 10:00 PT — we've created a calendar invite and included a short agenda (30 min presentation, 25 min Q&A, 5 min next steps). If your auditors need more time, we can extend.

Links to artifacts: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/SIG/Veridian/dossier ; https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1abcDEF (diagram quickview).

If you want any section tightened (shorter summary, expanded eviction playbook, or additional network telemetry screenshots) let us know and we'll update before final on Dec 10.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: segregation_summary_v1.pdf, private-dedicated-netmap.vsdx, sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx
